blocking.fix: In §§7.3/10, add an explicit ownership rule. Recommended conservative wording: “A run's device ownership footprint is the set of console, clock and block models referenced by the entry's transitive CC/R call closure. bennett_run acquires that footprint exclusively before execution and retains it until CLOSED, including while COMPLETED, FAILED or REVERSED. If another non-CLOSED run owns any model in the footprint, bennett_run returns E_INVALID_STATE before execution or any ownership acquisition. Entropy position and effect tapes are run-local and do not conflict. Runs with disjoint device footprints remain subject to the existing register and memory ownership rules.” In §14.3 T4, add: “For shared program state, restoration concerns the reversing run's owned components; disjoint components belonging to other runs remain unchanged.” Add the §15 overlap vector: B's initial launch is E_INVALID_STATE with no effects; after A is reversed and closed, retried B leaves console=5a; after A is closed unreversed, retried B leaves console=a55a. A second viable approach is a specified global device-dependency history with reverse-dependency ordering for both segment uncall and whole-run reversal, accompanied by revised eligibility rules. I recommend exclusive ownership because it preserves the existing local reversal machinery.
